title: A Paper Medal
subtitle: Fortune's blessings often come knocking on your door or window when you least expect them.

items.text: Hotel, Rayashki

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: The reserves of runium running dry, the appearance of new critters, the sudden snowstorm.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I've connected the ley lines of each of these phenomena. The map is nearly complete!
She unfolds the complex blueprint filled with various lines and marks.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: But still haven't traced many lines and marks back to their source.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Perhaps if I go back to the factories, into the restricted zones ... But, I can't do that alone.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Definitely not when the situation in town is so unstable.
Windsong collapses onto the table. An avalanche follows, covering her in layers of books and manuscripts.
The piles around her loom like a mountain range, casting her in shadow.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Well, I should have given this up long ago. There's no chance that the study of ley lines will ever be accepted again.
Phantom voices of past mockery and scorn rise up to her ears.

items.speaker: "Reviewer"
items.text: Regretfully, Ms. Windsong, with nothing but these outdated files and materials to back you up, there's simply no way to justify reinstating the study of ley lines into our curriculum.

items.speaker: "Reviewer"
items.text: We don't have unlimited funds, and we must save our money for projects with greater potential. The study of ley lines is ...

items.speaker: "Reviewer"
items.text: Of course, we might be able to consider new ideas and projects. You can't be allowed to do this on your own.

items.speaker: "Reviewer"
items.text: You will need endorsements from the Institution of Geographic Studies, the Arcane Creature Society, or other such organizations.

items.speaker: "Reviewer"
items.text: Let me think. Zeno seems to be interested in geographers recently. They've just recruited a number of researchers for a new commission. Maybe you should go try your luck with them.
An echo of a nursery rhyme rings out from beyond her self-made mountain range.
But she is all but oblivious to it.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: The submission date is getting closer each day, but I've made poor progress. Zeno won't endorse me if I can't find a breakthrough.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: They have become more and more radical and desperate lately. First, they sent those researchers here to conduct their haphazard studies, and now, an armed force.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: And all this effort just to chase the rumor of some source of "perpetual energy"?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: "That this perpetual energy source must be hidden somewhere beneath the permafrost!"

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: The higher-ups call the shots. All they need to do is spread a little honey in the right places. Then all the little researchers will swarm on it like flies.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: But could there really be a magical power source like that?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Whether there is or not, I still have a map to finish. There's no way that I can map every ley line in the region all by myself.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Goodbye research funds, goodbye lectures and seminars, and so long to my dreams of being chair of the "Geographical Perspectives" forum.
She jostles the heaps of books, moving them just enough to let in some light and sound.
They seep in through the cracks like starlight.
Took-took!
The door snaps shut. Windsong stands against it nervously.
Instruments roll off the table, colliding with each other on the windowsill, the corners, and under the bed, falling in a cacophonous disarray.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: What was that?
The door is gently pushed open again, revealing the curious face of a sunflower peeking in through the crack.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Ms. Windsong, we've been waiting for you!
As far as medals go, the design is a little cruder than expected, and damp paper doesn't quite have the same gravitas as gold or silver.
Still, Windsong has fantasized countless times about receiving such an accolade for her work, even a paper one.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: Ms. Windsong, we prepared a special medal ceremony for you and Avgust!

items.speaker: Pasono
items.text: Please come to our ceremony!

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: We just wanted to thank you for teaching us.

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: Ms. Vila was right. We shouldn't have been so quick to argue. We should have listened!

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: So you should be given an award for being right!

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: But our ceremony will not be as big as the ones on TV.
Indeed, this is a very special and exclusive reward.
Simple as it is, it comes with something nothing else could: the innocence and laughter of children.

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: Ms. Windsong, will you accept this medal?
For the first time in a long while, the study of ley lines basks in the glow of scholarly acclaim.
The paper medal is cupped in her trembling hands.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I have no cup to put this medal in, so we can't toast with it in celebration.
She sniffles.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: But now I know, no matter what, I won't be returning empty-handed. Thank you, kids.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: Do you mean, are you leaving us?

items.speaker: Pasono
items.text: But there is so much you still need to teach us!

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: "Rayashki embraces every guest," including you, Ms. Windsong—don't you like it here?
The children are on the verge of tears. She is pulled in helplessly, too.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: But those things I heard at the welcome ceremony ... Won't we all be leaving soon?

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: No! I don't believe it. That stranger was mean; he wasn't our friend!

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: Hmph. This is our town; they can't speak for us.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: That's right!
Neither doubt nor sorrow will dim their eyes—before her lies only a sea of steadfast faces.
Their words encouraging and powerful despite their youth.
They plant some strange seed of hope within her.

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: Ms. Vila "invited" the man from Zeno to leave his ship. Then they went into Mr. Evgeni's meeting room together.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: Uncle Knut promised me that no one will give up this place.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: They will go to many meetings and find "a solution that satisfies both sides."

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: The tortoises move slowly. They need to keep their eyes opened and look for a better answer!

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: So will you stay and teach us?

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: I won't cause you any more trouble, I promise!
The children burst into laughter.
Their voices very nearly drown out the rustling noises coming from the windowsill.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Mm? Comrade Calculator is speaking!
Curiosity propels the child through the half-open door of the guest room.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Hello!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Comrade Calculator, are you giving the earthworms directions?
The clamor by the window crescendos.
Even on tiptoes, the child barely reaches the faintly glowing calibrator.
Unfortunately, he is not the only one reaching for it.
*roars*
More unfortunate still, scaly claws prove mightier than little fingers.

items.speaker: "Ley Calibrator"
items.text: *cracks*
The other children notice the tug-of-war and crowd around Windsong, squeezing into the increasingly cramped room.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: What's going on here? Ah, my calibrator!
*chews*

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: The whale-like backbone, the diamond-shaped teeth, two short legs, with dim eyes, and an extremely sharp nose. That must be a Kikituk!

items.speaker: Kikituk
items.text: *gasps*

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: But their closest habitat should be Kong Karls Land, hundreds of kilometers away.
Its snout fixates on the new treat in Windsong's grasp.
She pulls out the scanner, its gears whining as ley lines flood forth.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Their marks on the map appear to be red, sort of reddish brown, and there's a large amount of ley energy accumulated around them. Clearly, they're high on the food chain.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Seems like the "small fish" have attracted more than one "big fish."
With a swift kick, she sends the grinning critter tumbling.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Kids, get behind me!
The undeterred Kikituks close in on the narrow ledge.

items.speaker: Kikituk
items.text: *hissing*

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Oh, oh! The Kikituks are giving a performance!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Their nose sings, their fur dances, and their belly shakes.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Mm?

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: But why aren't their ears doing anything?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Avgust! What are you doing there? Stay back; those are not Qiqirn!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: But, but ...
The meaning of both their messages is lost in the confusion.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: But, but their ears are left behind. They-they can't join the dance.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Then they will not get their Alenka!

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Ears?
Windsong, struck by her sudden revelation, fixes on the Kikituk's head.
Beneath its tufts of plush fur lie well-hidden ears of a deeper color.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Природа это числа и черты.
After a brief incantation, lines converge in a beam that hits precisely on its ear.

items.speaker: Kikituk
items.text: *wails*
The creature's cry pierces the air.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: So that seems to be their weak spot.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Good job, little one. You're even more perceptive than I thought!
Windsong pats Avgust's head.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Next ...
She reveals a dark and dangerous smile.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Hmph.
The Kikituks finally relinquish their ill-gotten gains, leaping down and away from the windowsill.
Leaving behind gnawed wet fragments of the ley calibrator.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: S**t! This was one of the last working instruments I had.
A sunflower gently pats against Windsong's shoulder.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Don't be sad, Ms. Windsong.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: If we plant them in the soil, many more will come out when spring comes.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Heh. Thank you, Avgust.

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: Ms. Windsong, can I be a ley hunter too?

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: If we were as good as you are, maybe we could've protected your machine.

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: And maybe we could protect our town.
Windsong turns her head, meeting many pairs of expectant eyes.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Kids, ley hunting isn't a good profession.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: If you become a ley hunter, you will have to deal with doubt from all your peers, even hatred, and homework that piles up to your roof.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: Ms. Windsong, people in Rayashki are taught not to doubt or hate others. They would never hate you, or us!

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: Exactly!
The children of Rayashki are in some ways so strange to her.
Their courage and solidarity overcome her long-standing hesitation.
Her curiosity at them, at all of this, becomes a palpable force.
One pulling her ever closer to Rayashki.
